_comment: Controls what the buying guides publish. Read at BUILD time by tools/build.py,
not at runtime — when a network is off its links are never written into the HTML
at all, rather than being hidden with CSS. Hiding them would leave competitor
affiliate links sitting in the page source of every product, which reads as
Flip it with:  python tools/site_toggle.py aliexpress on|off
Either way the site is rebuilt and redeployed, so a change is live in ~2 minutes.
israel covers local Israeli-store deals on the homepage feed. Amazon does
not require exclusivity, so these are kept by default — turn them off with
!site israel off if you want the homepage to be Amazon and nothing else.
_feed_comment: `feed` governs the HOMEPAGE grid. `affiliates` above governs the GUIDES.
They are separate on purpose — wiring them together once deleted 815 deals
from the homepage as a side effect of a guides-only change.
aliexpress_off_reason: Off since 2026-08-09 on the reasoning that a page leading with a competing marketplace on every product is a needless reason to be refused. NOTE 2026-08-14: that was written as though an application were under review. None has been submitted, so this is currently switched off against a review that is not happening — turning AliExpress links off in the guides costs real commission for no present benefit. Decide deliberately: leave off until the day you apply, or turn back on with 'python tools/site_toggle.py aliexpress on'.
amazon_associate_note: not_applied -> pending on the day the application is actually submitted -> approved the day the acceptance email arrives. This read 'pending' from 2026-08-09 to 2026-08-14 while nothing had been submitted, and the site said so out loud in all six languages: the footer read 'We have applied to the Amazon Associates Program.' Claiming an application you have not made is the same kind of false statement as claiming a membership you do not hold, on the very site Amazon reads when you do apply. The copy now says only what is true either way — not an Associate, nothing earned from Amazon links.
_amazon_pa_content_comment: Whether Amazon price / list price / rating / review count / product image are
published. Under the Associates Operating Agreement that content is PA-API-only,
and there are no PA-API keys yet, so true here means publishing it without one.
Owner's decision, 2026-08-14, made with the risk stated: the site should show
Amazon working — real products, real photos, real prices — so that a reviewer
can see the site can do the job, on the reasoning that a rejection can be
answered by switching this to false and reapplying.
Worth knowing when weighing that: a rejection before approval is cheap to fix,
but a policy closure AFTER approval is much harder to undo. If the acceptance
email arrives, set this to false the same day and leave it false until
AMAZON_PAAPI_* keys exist — see HANDOFF.md, 'After acceptance'.
PA-API keys always win: once they exist this flag stops mattering, because the
true  -> publish        false -> withhold until PA-API
